summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder with urostomy, type 2 diabetes, and bilateral lower extremity amputations due to frostbite was admitted for chills and suspected sepsis. She presented with cloudy urine and was somnolent on arrival, with lab findings showing leukocytosis, elevated CRP, and metabolic acidosis. IV antibiotics were started, and she was transitioned to oral sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. The patient declined all diagnostic testing, including CT and ultrasound, and refused full wound and abdominal examinations. She improved subjectively and requested discharge on hospital day three, leaving against medical advice. She was prescribed antibiotics and gabapentin, with strong recommendations to follow up with wound care at a respite program and her primary care provider.
